name: Tetrahedral Strips and Fans
definition: Two new primitives introduced to address the bandwidth bottleneck between main memory and the graphics processor, allowing performance improvements in rendering tetrahedral meshes similar to triangle strips and fans for triangle meshes. They make a software sorting pass unnecessary by moving computations for order-independent transparency and volume scan conversion to graphics hardware.
summary: Tetrahedral Strips and Fans are graphics primitives that reduce memory bandwidth by grouping tetrahedra into sequences, enabling 72 to 85 times faster volumetric rendering than triangle-based approaches.
